question: Where is memory content (intact against twin facts) lost in V19's frozen dual-budget pipeline: in the written memory, in the read output, or on the way to the native head?
extraction_checks: V19 receipts and checkpoint bodies match their pinned hashes
the initial state is rebuilt by V19's code and matches V19's INITIAL fingerprint
store receipts (renderings, spans, contexts) equal V19's for both splits
the pipeline residual equals the recomputed common + workspace parts exactly
zero memory reproduces the frozen direct base exactly
reader queries do not depend on memory

endpoints.memory: On the 128 held-out worlds (256 affected pairs), the attention probe's content following (both sides right) beats both the zeroed-memory and the shuffled-memory probe, each by a one-sided sign test over worlds at p <= alpha, in every probe seed.
endpoints.reading: The primary route's contrast probe (intact minus twin read output, predicting the intact answer) beats chance by a one-sided sign test over held-out worlds (two affected questions each) at p <= alpha.
endpoints.transport: Known from V19: the FP64 intended answer-gap change is donor-directed for 129 of 256 held-out questions and no published answer flips.
endpoints.verdict_rule: memory fails: CONTENT_ABSENT_IN_MEMORY; memory passes and reading fails: LOST_IN_READING; both pass: LOST_IN_TRANSPORT. One verdict per state.

descriptive: probe accuracy on all held-out rows, per probe and control
contrast-probe accuracy for the common route and the total residual
form control: the same contrast probe on intact minus reverse_intact (same facts, reversed order)
distinguishability: median |intact - twin| / |intact - reverse_intact| for memory and each route
process_policy: each role a fresh process through scripts/run_source_sealed.py, in order, stopping at the first failure
scope: Probes of a frozen, historical pipeline. A pass says the content is extractable from that rung by these small probes; a fail says these probes could not extract it. No workspace training, no answer changes, no claim about memory use by the native model.
